# Plain A11y

> A free, open-source Chrome extension (MIT) that checks the open page for accessibility problems and explains each one in plain language: what is wrong, who it affects, how to fix it and which role should handle it (design, content or code). It uses the axe-core engine, runs entirely in the browser, and collects and sends nothing.

Plain A11y is made for designers, content editors, product managers and QA people who are not accessibility specialists. Automated checking finds only part of the accessibility problems: an empty result does not mean a page is accessible, and the extension says so.

## Install

- [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/plain-a11y/cnldihaficjignkhpgodanceilllbjfb): add Plain A11y to Chrome (free, no account)

## Pages

- [Home](https://a11y-ext.bereg.dev/): what the extension does, how it works, what it covers and what it does not, install steps, questions
- [Privacy policy](https://a11y-ext.bereg.dev/privacy): the extension collects nothing and sends nothing; the three permissions (activeTab, scripting, storage) and why
- [License](https://a11y-ext.bereg.dev/license): MIT License and third-party notices (axe-core is MPL-2.0)
